newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: No Swazi talks after government fails to show.
newsitem.headline: No Swazi talks after government fails to show.

text.p: Scheduled talks to address Swaziland trade union demands for democracy in the landlocked kingdom collapsed on Wednesday when the government failed to turn up, a unionist said.
Swaziland Federation of Trade Unions (SFTU) official Sipho Mamba said the government delegation sent a letter late on Wednesday saying they never received an agenda for the talks.
"It looks like the government is playing hide and seek. It looks like they don't care about what happened in the past. They did not get the message from the stayaway," Mamba told Reuters.
Government sources were not available for comment.
A nationwide strike, called a month ago by the federation to force the government to speed up democratic reform, ended on Wednesday when workers returned to the hard-hit sugar and timber industries.
The unions have given the government a list of 27 demands that include the repeal of a 1973 royal decree that vested all state powers in the monarchy and banned political parties.
Business sources said the federation had "shot itself in the foot" by enforcing a blockade of the country's borders on Monday, which weakened its bargaining position.
The SFTU, the mighty Congress of South African Trade Unions (Cosatu) and Mozambican unions prevented goods moving in and out of the kingdom in the day-long action.

"The blockade has obviously antagonised the government and it lost the unions a lot of its support from ordinary Swazis because of the outside interference from Cosatu, which was strongly objected to here," the business source said.
The cost of the month-long stayaway is estimated at well over 100 million rand ($23 million), the source said.
King Mswati III has set up a constitutional review commission to make recommendations on setting up a constitutional democracy. The process will take two years.
